title: F.H.E.D donates to twenty-eight people living with disabilities at the Palace
excerpt: In the courtyard of the Guneku Palace on 16 December 2021, Fons for Health, Education and Development distributed birds, feed, wheelchairs and medication worth 1,381,000 FCFA to twenty-eight people living with disabilities.
sourceNote: Community record — Mbengwi Online (Facebook group and blog), reported by Fongoh P. Ayeh. Written fresh from the reported facts and attributed; no text or photograph of theirs is reproduced. Recorded 2026-09-02.
body:
On Thursday 16 December 2021, in the courtyard of the Guneku Palace, F.H.E.D — Fons for Health, Education and Development made a donation to twenty-eight people living with disabilities from Guneku and neighbouring villages.

The donation comprised 220 table birds, 22 bags of feed, four wheelchairs and anti-epilepsy medication, with a total value of 1,381,000 FCFA. Nine days earlier the organisation had donated eight benches, worth 200,000 FCFA, to the Presbyterian School Annex at Ku.

Present at the Palace ceremony were Ndingwan Primus, Chairman of the Guneku Traditional Council; Fomuki Carine, a queen of the Palace; and Fons of neighbouring Fondoms.

F.H.E.D is headquartered in the Guneku Palace. It was founded in 2003 as Fons Against AIDS, with HRH Fon Fomuki Patrick Nji of Guneku as its founding president, and renamed in 2021 when its mandate widened beyond HIV and AIDS.

Beneficiaries are not named here. The source identifies individuals by their disability, and that is not ours to publish.
